card.title: We Learned to Win Together
card.instruction: Treat your memories of competing side by side as proof that you still understand one another better than anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Remember our relay signal? Two taps meant you needed me to take over.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're racing against each other today. I just want a fair start.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said that before our county final. You needed a minute to breathe.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My daughter thinks I'm nervous because she's watching.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She's missed the ankle bounce. That's your winning leg warming up. I've seen it bring us home.

mechanism: A treats shared relay history as proof of superior understanding of B's present body language.
confusable: Unlike nostalgia, memories must authorize a current reading of B above another observer's reading.
comparison: S199-a reads a former teammate's nerves through bodily signals; S199-b uses old quiz patterns to offer time.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
